introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: The forces $\mathbf{F}_1 = (2\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$ and $\mathbf{F}_2 = (\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$ act at points with position vectors $\mathbf{r}_1 = (\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$ and $\mathbf{r}_2 = \lambda(2\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$ respectively. Given that the lines of action of $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ intersect at the point with position vector $(5\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j} - p\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$, find
incertitudes: Question 1 (i) : avec le signe imprimé « - pk », la composante en k du point d'intersection vaut 7, donc p = -7 (valeur négative). Le corrigé le démontre par les deux droites d'action (qui concordent) et ne modifie pas l'énoncé.

Question 1 (ii) : le sujet imprime « (5 marks) » pour la force F0 et le couple G, puis « (2 marks) » sur une ligne séparée pour « Find also, the magnitude of the couple G ». Cette dernière demande est transcrite comme sous-question distincte « iii » (2 points) ; la sous-question « ii » (5 points) ne demande que F0 et G.

questions.enonce_markdown: the values of the constants $\lambda$ and $p$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Line of action of $\mathbf{F}_1$.** It passes through the point with position vector $\mathbf{r}_1$ and has direction $\mathbf{F}_1$:

$$\mathbf{r} = (\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}) + s(2\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k}).$$

It goes through $(5, 6, -p)$, so

$$1 + 2s = 5,\qquad 2 + 2s = 6,\qquad 1 + 3s = -p.$$

The first two equations both give $s = 2$ (they agree), and then $-p = 1 + 3(2) = 7$, so $p = -7$.

**Line of action of $\mathbf{F}_2$.** It passes through $\mathbf{r}_2 = \lambda(2\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k})$ with direction $\mathbf{F}_2 = \mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$:

$$\mathbf{r} = \lambda(2\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k}) + t(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}).$$

Through $(5, 6, 7)$:

$$2\lambda + t = 5,\qquad 2\lambda + 2t = 6,\qquad 3\lambda + t = 7.$$

Subtracting the first two equations gives $t = 1$, hence $2\lambda = 4$ and $\lambda = 2$. The third equation is then satisfied: $3(2) + 1 = 7$. So the two lines really do meet, at $(5, 6, 7)$.

$$\boxed{\lambda = 2,\qquad p = -7}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: the force $\mathbf{F}_0$ through the origin $O$ and the couple $\mathbf{G}$ which are together equivalent to these forces. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $\lambda = 2$ we have $\mathbf{r}_2 = 4\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 6\mathbf{k}$.

**The force through $O$.** It must have the same resultant as the two forces:

$$\mathbf{F}_0 = \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{F}_2 = (2 + 1)\mathbf{i} + (2 + 2)\mathbf{j} + (3 + 1)\mathbf{k} = 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N}.$$

**The couple.** The couple $\mathbf{G}$ must equal the total moment of the original forces about $O$ (the moment of $\mathbf{F}_0$ about $O$ is zero):

$$\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{r}_1 \times \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{r}_2 \times \mathbf{F}_2.$$

$$\mathbf{r}_1 \times \mathbf{F}_1 = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = (6 - 2)\mathbf{i} - (3 - 2)\mathbf{j} + (2 - 4)\mathbf{k} = 4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k},$$

$$\mathbf{r}_2 \times \mathbf{F}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 4 & 4 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = (4 - 12)\mathbf{i} - (4 - 6)\mathbf{j} + (8 - 4)\mathbf{k} = -8\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}.$$

$$\mathbf{G} = -4\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N\,m}.$$

**Check.** Each force can be moved along its line of action to the common point $(5, 6, 7)$ without changing its moment about $O$: $(5\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j} + 7\mathbf{k}) \times \mathbf{F}_1 = 4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k}$ and $(5\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j} + 7\mathbf{k}) \times \mathbf{F}_2 = -8\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}$, the same two vectors.

$$\boxed{\mathbf{F}_0 = 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N},\qquad \mathbf{G} = -4\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N\,m}}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Find also the magnitude of the couple $\mathbf{G}$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From part (ii), $\mathbf{G} = -4\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N\,m}$, so

$$|\mathbf{G}| = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + 1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{21} \approx 4.58\ \mathrm{N\,m}.$$

(Remark: $\mathbf{G} \cdot \mathbf{F}_0 = -12 + 4 + 8 = 0$, as expected because the two forces intersect, so they reduce to a single force through $(5, 6, 7)$ and the couple is perpendicular to the resultant.)

$$\boxed{|\mathbf{G}| = \sqrt{21}\ \mathrm{N\,m} \approx 4.58\ \mathrm{N\,m}}$$
